transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess what finally made me come in is I keep finding myself getting up during things where I really should just stay seated. Like sprint planning meetings, or calls about the mortgage. I’ll suddenly “need” water or decide I have to check something in the other room. It’s not a huge thing, but it’s been noticeable.
When you get up during those meetings or calls, is it because staying seated starts to make you feel intensely anxious or unbearably uncomfortable?

Not anxious, exactly. It’s more like… there’s this pressure inside, like I need to move or switch to something else. Even if I look calm, I’m sort of fighting the urge to do something with my hands or get up.
Did you have this same kind of trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I remember in elementary school teachers would move my desk sometimes, or remind me to stay seated. I’d pop up a lot, or talk before they called on me. And I guess I rushed through work even when I knew how to do it.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations, even when you want to pay attention?

Yeah… sometimes. I’ll start reviewing a pull request or reading mortgage papers and I mean to focus, but a few minutes later I’m just staring at the same paragraph and thinking about five other things. Then I have to pull myself back.
When your mind drifts during tasks like reviewing a pull request or reading mortgage papers, is it usually because you’re caught up in worry?
Not usually worry, no. It’s more like I mean to focus, and then a few minutes later I notice I’m still on the same section, but my mind’s gone off in five different directions.
Have these attention and restlessness problems caused real difficulties for you at work, at home, or in relationships?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like everything is falling apart, but it’s been causing some friction. At work and at home, people have to follow up with me more than they used to, and I don’t like that. I worry I’m starting to seem like the unreliable one with planning things, even though I’m really trying.
